name: table-count
description: Number of Drizzle pgTable() definitions across shared/. The mature-machine north star is a SMALLER schema (<=450 tables); today's count is far above it. This strict down-only ratchet makes the schema monotonic: adding a table fails CI until the baseline is deliberately bumped (a conscious 'yes we need this'), and every consolidation lowers the baseline toward the target. Founder-chosen 'strict' 2026-07-16.
lastBumpNote: 756 -> 753 on 2026-07-29: platform money-custody purge (founder ruling "be the rail, not the provider", migration 0214). transaction_fee_settlements, fee_payout_schedules and fee_audit_log were the storage for server/services/transactionFeeService.ts — a platform escrow-and-take-a-cut engine (collect a buyer/seller/platform fee, HOLD it on AcreOS's balance for N days, release, transfer out) that had ZERO call sites. Nothing ever wrote a row and nothing ever read one, and processPayout() stamped a fabricated `tr_simulated_<ts>` id into a money column. Customer money never moves on AcreOS's own account, so the tables have no future either: dropped rather than frozen. A REDUCTION, which this ratchet's own rule requires be locked in the same commit. PRIOR NOTE — 754 -> 756 on 2026-07-29: ach_mandates + ach_debit_attempts (founder ruling #12(c) Wave C — ACH mandate/autopay, migration 0213). The borrower portal shipped an autopay Switch that wrote ONE boolean (notes.auto_pay_enabled) and scheduled nothing; the flag's only reader was cashFlowForecaster, which FORECAST money that was never collected while the portal told the borrower "Autopay is on — we will collect this payment automatically". Two things a boolean cannot carry each need a table. (1) ach_mandates: NACHA §2.3 requires the Originator to obtain AND RETAIN the Receiver's authorization for every consumer debit and produce it on demand — the verbatim text shown, its version, agreed_at, IP/UA, the dollar ceiling and frequency authorized, and the processor's corroborating mandate id. A rollup column cannot answer "what exactly did this borrower authorize, and when". (2) ach_debit_attempts: one row per (note, period, attempt), where the unique index IS the double-charge guard — a duplicate job run, a double-click, or a crash-and-retry all lose the insert BEFORE money moves, and the same key is replayed as the processor idempotency key. Return codes (R01-R29), the bounded re-presentment ladder, and the reversal linkage all hang off the attempt, so a returned debit is auditable instead of a mutated status. Deliberate bump per this ratchet's own procedure. PRIOR NOTE — 753 -> 754 on 2026-07-29: note_payoff_quotes (Wave C 'Money moves', migration 0212). A payoff statement is a representation the note holder is legally bound by, and AcreOS computed payoff quotes in three places — with three different day-count behaviours — while persisting NONE of them. When a closer wires the quoted figure and the ledger disagrees to the cent, nothing recorded what was quoted, as of what date, or from which inputs, so there was no way to establish which side moved. No rollup column can answer that; the quote EVENT (full engine input snapshot alongside its output, immutable, one row per quote issued) needs a table. It deliberately spans BOTH note books via note_system + note_ref, so unifying the borrower-portal quote onto the same engine needs no second table. Deliberate bump per this ratchet's own procedure. PRIOR NOTE — 752 -> 753 on 2026-07-29: mail_qr_scan_events (Wave B 'Wire the engine', migration 0211). The direct-mail attribution funnel was a capable-looking UI over permanent zeros — qr_scan_count was read in 8 places and written in 0, with no QR generation and no scan endpoint. The rollup column alone cannot answer 'why is this number what it is', and a QR redirect that silently swallows bot/prefetch hits without recording them is just a different kind of unaccountable number, so the scan EVENTS (counted and deliberately-not-counted alike, each with a reason) get a table. Everything else in that migration is additive columns/indexes on existing tables. Deliberate bump per this ratchet's own procedure. PRIOR NOTE — 747 -> 752 on 2026-07-29: abTestOutcomes/marketWatchlist persistence tables (founder ruling #12(c) Wave A — 'Nothing lies': three shipped features ran on in-memory Maps that vanished on every restart). Deliberate bump per this ratchet's own procedure. The five: market_watchlist_entries, market_watchlist_alerts, outreach_ab_tests, outreach_ab_outcomes (T117 + T22), plus investor_verification_requests for the KYC state machine ported in the same wave.
